protocol: Routine Navy aviation training with 9 min at 25,000 ft.
outcome_window: Retro-orbital pain during descent resolved approximately 7 h after exposure. Pain and blurred vision recurred on 4 June, with presentation on 6 June.
locator: Case Report pp. 985–986 and Discussion pp. 988–989
note: Authors evaluated possible recurrent untreated DCS and concurrent sinusitis. The presentation date is distinct from initial onset and recurrence.

protocol: Japan Air Self-Defense Force Type III indoctrination. Symptoms began near 30,000 ft during ascent. The patient transferred to the entry chamber and descended to 25,000 ft; other cadets continued to 38,000 ft.
outcome_window: Symptoms resolved at ground level. No recurrence during the source's 24-hour follow-up.
note: Attending initially considered neurological DCS. Author concluded probable cutaneous bends with atopic dermatitis. The achieved peak of this individual is not specified exactly.

protocol: Pilot-candidate training with about 15 min at 35,000 ft and about 1 h for the entire chamber exposure.
outcome_window: Emergency transfer about 2 h after training with chest pain and dyspnea. The Discussion also places symptoms about 2 h after decompression.
note: Authors attributed cardiac findings to coronary gas embolism after decompression. Direct demonstration of coronary gas is unavailable.

protocol: C.I.M.A. chamber training. Thirty minutes of sea-level oxygen prebreathe and 1 min at the 30,000-ft peak, followed by descent and a hypoxia exercise at 25,000 ft.
outcome_window: Acute symptoms in the chamber. The abstract gives 28,000 ft, while the Case Report describes symptoms after the 25,000-ft exercise and resumption of oxygen.
locator: Abstract and Case Report pp. 1025–1026 and Discussion pp. 1027–1028
note: Presumptive cerebral arterial gas embolism, per source. The 30,000-ft field is attained maximum altitude. The exact onset altitude is unresolved.

protocol: Authors' abstract describes more than 2,400 chamber ascents among 130 volunteers using different decompression tables.
